The officer inside the Trotwood Cruiser that was crushed in the collision, Officer Michael Richardson survived the impact. But the crash left him with severe injuries and lasting psychological trauma. Richardson developed PTSD from the incident and ultimately never returned to duty. The suspect was identified as James Michael Scurvin. Skirvin would go on to survive the incident as well. He was shot multiple times, pulled from the wreckage and given CPR by officers until medics arrived and transported him to the hospital. Skirvin was charged with a long list of offenses, including multiple counts of felonious assault on peace officers, aggravated menacing, vehicular assault, failure to comply, discharging a firearm improper handling of a firearm, aggravated possession of drugs, and the original felonious assault and domestic violence charges for attacking his daughter. In April of 2025, a jury found him guilty on nearly every count. The judge imposed a sentence of 58 to 63 and a half years in prison, ensuring he will spend the rest of his life behind bars.
